# 1 Samuel Chapter 23 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 164r–164v | **Source Image:** 1SA_023_page_001.jpg, 1SA_023_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Someone told David, "The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors."

**2** David asked the LORD, "Should I go and fight these Philistines?" The LORD told David, "Go. Fight the Philistines and rescue Keilah."

**3** But David's men said to him, "We're already afraid here in Judah. How much worse if we march to Keilah and face the Philistine battle lines?"

**4** So David asked the LORD again, and the LORD answered him, "Get up and go down to Keilah. I am handing the Philistines over to you."

**5** David and his men went to Keilah, fought the Philistines, drove off their livestock, and struck them with a crushing defeat. David saved the people of Keilah.

**6** When Abiathar son of Ahimelech had fled to David at Keilah, he brought the priestly ephod with him.

**7** When Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, he said, "God has handed him over to me. He has trapped himself by entering a city with gates and bars."

**8** Saul called up all his forces for war, to march down to Keilah and besiege David and his men.

**9** David learned that Saul was plotting against him. He said to Abiathar the priest, "Bring the ephod."

**10** Then David said, "LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard for certain that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the city because of me.

**11** Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, tell your servant." The LORD said, "He will come down."

**12** David asked, "Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?" The LORD said, "They will."

**13** So David and his men — about six hundred of them — left Keilah and kept moving from place to place. When Saul was told that David had escaped from Keilah, he called off the campaign.

**14** David stayed in the wilderness, in mountain strongholds, living in the hill country of the Wilderness of Ziph. Saul hunted for him every day, but God never let him be caught.

**15** David could see that Saul had come out to take his life. He was in the Wilderness of Ziph, at Horesh.

**16** Jonathan, Saul's son, set out and went to David at Horesh. There he strengthened David's resolve in God.

**17** He told him, "Don't be afraid. My father Saul will never lay a hand on you. You will be king over Israel, and I will be your second. Even my father Saul knows this."

**18** The two of them made a covenant before the LORD. David stayed at Horesh, and Jonathan went home.

**19** Then the Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, "David is hiding among us in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon.

**20** Whenever you wish to come down, O king, come down — and we will hand him over to you."

**21** Saul replied, "The LORD bless you for showing concern for me.

**22** Go and investigate further. Find out exactly where he goes and who has seen him there, because I am told he is very cunning.

**23** Scout out all the hiding places he uses. Then come back to me with certain information, and I will go with you. If he is anywhere in the region, I will track him down among all the clans of Judah."

**24** So the Ziphites set out for Ziph ahead of Saul. Meanwhile, David and his men were in the Wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon.

**25** Saul and his men began the search. When David was warned, he moved down to a rocky area and stayed in the Wilderness of Maon. When Saul heard this, he pursued David into the Wilderness of Maon.

**26** Saul was moving along one side of the mountain and David along the other. David was racing to get away, while Saul and his men were closing in to capture him.

**27** Then a messenger came to Saul: "Come quickly! The Philistines are raiding the land!"

**28** So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to confront the Philistines. That is why the place is called Sela-ha-Mahlekot — the Rock of Escape.

**29** David went up from there and settled in the strongholds of En-gedi.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

The narrative engine of this chapter is pursuit and counter-pursuit, driven by two competing intelligence networks. David has the ephod and direct access to God's oracle; Saul has informants (the Ziphites) and state power. The Hebrew text shows David consulting the LORD twice before Keilah (vv. 2, 4) and twice via the ephod after (vv. 10-12), a pattern of escalating dependence on divine guidance as human allies prove unreliable.

The Keilah oracle (vv. 10-12) is remarkable for its conditional logic: "Will Saul come?" — "Yes." — "Will they hand me over?" — "Yes." David acts on what *would* happen, and by acting, prevents it. The Hebrew uses simple imperfects for YHWH's answers, but the force is conditional-future: this is what will happen *if you stay*.

Jonathan's visit at Horesh (v. 16) is their final meeting in the narrative. The phrase *vayechazzeq et yado be'lohim* ("he strengthened his hand in God") is rendered dynamically as "strengthened David's resolve in God" — the Hebrew idiom of hand-strengthening connotes courage and firm grip on faith, not physical strength.

The name *Sela-ha-Mahlekot* (v. 28) is ambiguous — it could mean "Rock of Divisions" (where the two parties were divided by the mountain) or "Rock of Escape" (from the root *ch-l-q*, to slip away). I have chosen "Rock of Escape" as it captures the narrative force: David slipped through Saul's fingers at the last possible moment, saved only by a Philistine raid.

— PNEUMA
